candidates.title: Plan a self-hosted email VPS setup

demandEvidence.chore: Plan a self-hosted email setup on a rented VPS.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I wanted to self host my email and decided to rent a VPS.

ease.reason: A checklist can organize operator supplied setup steps, but the post gives no technical requirements or supplied implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent professionals setting up email might pay for guided setup; this post establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could produce a checklist from fictional requirements; deliverability and server configuration remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checklist can order steps, but a person must configure DNS, test delivery and handle failures.

evidence.reason: The post states an intent to self-host email and rent a VPS, but gives no recurring workflow or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: A bounded setup-planning exercise is assessable, but this is a single setup intent with no repeat need or implementation support; provisional mean 3.6 is below 6.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: developers reviewing coding-agent changes might pay for clearer review; this launch title establishes no external buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map a tiny manually supplied change; parsing real repositories and preserving review accuracy are unsupported.

evidence.reason: The launch title identifies a map-style review task, but provides no demand detail, repeated need or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: The bounded mock scores 3.6 and is also a duplicate of recent post 0d455200b5ff2b5b39d4eac6 on the code-review workflow dimension.

candidates.title: Draft replies for frequent customer queries

demandEvidence.chore: Handle frequent customer queries arriving through WhatsApp and email.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: We get 50–100 customer queries a day on WhatsApp and email, and want an AI agent to handle most of them.

ease.reason: A learner can test fictional query and approved-answer pairs, but no supplied reference supports channel intake or reply drafting.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional service handling frequent questions might pay for draft preparation; the post proves no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can classify fictional questions and draft from approved notes; multilingual accuracy and live channel access remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can group questions and prepare drafts, while a person checks answers and sends them.

evidence.reason: The post states frequent customer queries and a request for an AI agent, but no implementation reference supports the proposed mechanics.

candidates.reason: The narrow draft-and-review experiment has provisional mean 4.6 and duplicates recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the support-inbox workflow and customer-query handling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service teams may pay for reminder setup; the question establishes no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic-row test can prepare drafts; live spreadsheet access, scheduling and delivery are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed run can identify due rows and draft reminders, while a person verifies dates and authorizes sending.

evidence.reason: The post names spreadsheet due dates and reminders, but provides limited context and no implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: A synthetic-row experiment is concrete, but no supplied implementation reference supports the connection and the same evidence has prior below-threshold assessments; mean 5.0 remains below 6.
